definition: Austere means very bare, plain, and without comfort or luxury — sometimes describing a strict, self-denying way of living.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word austere. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know austere should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The monastery cell was austere: stone walls, a narrow cot, and a single candle.
A plain room simply lacks decoration; an austere one feels deliberately stripped down to the bare minimum.
Austere describes severe plainness; ascetic goes even further, describing a life that rejects all comfort and pleasure as a discipline.

Spartan describes rooms, gear, and lifestyles stripped to the bare essentials, with a nod to toughness — a spartan bunkroom, a spartan training camp. Austere covers the same bareness but adds a colder, more forbidding edge, and it can also describe strict self-denial. Spartan feels practical; austere can feel forbidding.

Stark means harshly bare in a way that jumps out at you, and it especially describes blunt, unsoftened clarity — a stark outline, a stark contrast, a stark choice or warning. Austere describes bare places and strict living; stark describes how brutally plain and clear-cut something appears.

Severe means strict and unsparing, without softness — a severe teacher, a severe haircut, severe rules. Austere leans toward bareness and lack of comfort in places and lifestyles, while severe leans toward sternness in people, style, and discipline. An austere room lacks comfort; a severe one glares at you.
